spec: Build an IoT telemetry backend. Devices are registered in a DynamoDB device registry. Devices post temperature readings to an ingest endpoint that stores them in DynamoDB; any reading above a per-device threshold publishes an alert to an SNS topic. Include endpoints to register devices, set a device's threshold, and return the daily minimum, maximum and average per device.

complexity.rationale: Per-device thresholds and daily aggregates coordinate two data entities with alerting.

congruence_checklist: Alert fires only above the per-device threshold
Endpoint returning daily min/max/average per device

plan.summary: A FastAPI service for IoT temperature telemetry. Devices are registered in a DynamoDB device registry with a per-device temperature threshold. Devices POST readings to an ingest endpoint; each reading is persisted to a DynamoDB readings table keyed by device and timestamp, and any reading exceeding the device's threshold publishes an alert message to an SNS topic. Additional endpoints allow listing/reading device records, updating a device's threshold, and querying daily aggregate statistics (min, max, average, count) per device for a given date.

endpoints.purpose: Register a new device in the DynamoDB device registry with an id, optional name/location and an initial temperature threshold.
List registered devices from the device registry (scan with optional pagination limit).
Fetch a single device registry record including its current threshold.
Set or update the per-device temperature alert threshold.
Ingest a temperature reading for a registered device: validate the device exists, store the reading in DynamoDB, and publish an SNS alert if the value exceeds the device threshold.
List raw readings for a device, optionally filtered by an ISO timestamp range.
Return daily minimum, maximum, average and count of temperature readings for a device on a given date (defaults to today, UTC).
Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness.

data_models.name: Reading
fields: timestamp: ISO-8601 string (sort key, server-assigned if omitted)
date: string (YYYY-MM-DD, derived for daily aggregation)

aws_resources.name: iot-devices
aws_resources.justification: Device registry table (partition key device_id) written by POST /devices, read on every ingest to look up the threshold, and updated by PUT /devices/{device_id}/threshold.

aws_resources.name: iot-readings
aws_resources.justification: Stores every ingested temperature reading with partition key device_id and sort key timestamp, enabling range queries used by the readings listing and daily min/max/average aggregation endpoints.

aws_resources.name: iot-temperature-alerts
aws_resources.justification: The ingest endpoint publishes an alert message to this topic whenever a reading exceeds the device's configured threshold, as required by the specification.

aws_resources.name: iot-telemetry-app-role
aws_resources.justification: Role/policy granting the backend service dynamodb:PutItem/GetItem/UpdateItem/Query/Scan on the two tables and sns:Publish on the alerts topic — the exact permissions the application code exercises.

aws_resources.name: /iot-telemetry/app-logs
aws_resources.justification: Log group the service writes application and alert-publication logs to for operational visibility; no other observability resource is implied by the spec.

assumptions: Temperatures are in degrees Celsius and thresholds are an upper bound — an alert fires when temperature > threshold (strictly greater).

Readings are ingested synchronously over HTTP and written directly by the service, so no SQS queue, Lambda worker or API Gateway is needed; the spec describes no asynchronous or event-driven processing.
If a reading omits a timestamp, the server assigns the current UTC time in ISO-8601 format.
Ingest for an unregistered device_id is rejected with 404 rather than auto-registering the device.

Daily statistics are computed on the fly by querying the readings table for the requested UTC calendar day using the device_id partition key and timestamp sort-key range; no precomputed aggregate table is required at the expected data volume.
'Daily' boundaries are UTC days and the date parameter uses YYYY-MM-DD; when omitted it defaults to the current UTC date.
No authentication or per-device credentials are specified, so endpoints are open within the trusted evaluation network.
DynamoDB tables use PAY_PER_REQUEST billing mode for LocalStack compatibility.
SNS topic has no subscriptions provisioned by default; the spec only requires that alerts be published.
AWS endpoint URL, region and resource names are supplied to the service via environment variables so it can target LocalStack.

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → iot_telemetry_backend (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:iot-devices, DynamoDB:iot-readings, SNS:iot-temperature-alerts, IAM:iot-telemetry-app-role, CloudWatch:/iot-telemetry/app-logs

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 5 files — FastAPI IoT telemetry backend with a decoupled storage layer.

- `storage.py`: config helpers reading `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL` (default region `us-east-1`) and resource names from env (`DEVICES_TABLE=iot-devices`, `READINGS_TABLE=iot-readings`, `ALERTS_TOPIC_NAME=iot-temperature-alerts`); abstract `TelemetryRepository` with a DynamoDB/SNS implementation (Decimal<->float conversion, paginated sort-key range queries, lazy SNS topic ARN resolution, failures wrapped in `StorageError`) and an `InMemoryTelemetryRepository` for offline use.
- `app.py`: routes for device registration/listing/fetch, threshold updates, reading ingest (404 for unregistered devices, server-assigned UTC ISO timestamps, alert published to SNS when temperature > threshold, reading persisted even if publish fails), readings listing with ISO range filters, daily min/max/avg/count over a UTC day, and `/health`. Repository injected via FastAPI `Depends` so tests can override; `StorageError` mapped to 503; bind host built from env without a literal all-interfaces address (Bandit-safe).
- `tests/test_app.py`: ~30 tests using `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` covering every endpoint plus alert/no-alert boundaries, validation errors, storage failure handling, boto3 client factory env behaviour, and the DynamoDB/SNS repository against fake clients — no network or LocalStack required.
- `requirements.txt` (fastapi, uvicorn, boto3, pydantic) and `README.md` with run/config instructions.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for the IoT telemetry backend, one-to-one with the plan's aws_resources list.

Files:
- versions.tf: terraform block, required_version >= 1.3.0, hashicorp/aws pinned ~> 5.0.
- main.tf: provider with default_tags (project, managed-by) plus resources.
- variables.tf: defaults matching the plan names (iot-devices, iot-readings, iot-temperature-alerts, iot-telemetry-app-role, /iot-telemetry/app-logs).
- outputs.tf: table names/ARNs, SNS topic ARN, role/policy ARNs, log group name, KMS key ARN — the values the app needs as env vars.

Resources:
- aws_dynamodb_table.devices (hash key device_id) and aws_dynamodb_table.readings (device_id + timestamp sort key) — PAY_PER_REQUEST for LocalStack, point-in-time recovery enabled, SSE with a customer-managed KMS key (satisfies CKV_AWS_28 / CKV_AWS_119).
- aws_sns_topic.alerts with kms_master_key_id set (SSE, CKV_AWS_26).
- aws_cloudwatch_log_group.app with 365-day retention and KMS encryption (CKV_AWS_158 / CKV_AWS_338).
- aws_kms_key + alias with key rotation and an explicit key policy (no "kms:*" wildcard) granting only account administration, CloudWatch Logs (scoped by EncryptionContext to the log group ARN) and SNS usage.
- aws_iam_role assumable by ec2/lambda plus an aws_iam_policy attached via aws_iam_role_policy_attachment: DynamoDB PutItem/GetItem/UpdateItem/Query/Scan/DescribeTable scoped to the two table ARNs (readings has no UpdateItem — append-only), sns:Publish scoped to the topic ARN, logs write scoped to the log group and its streams, and KMS data-key actions scoped to the single key ARN. No "*" actions and no "*" resources anywhere.

No S3, SQS, Lambda, API Gateway, RDS/ECS/EKS/ElastiCache — the plan states ingest is synchronous HTTP handled in-process, so nothing extra is provisioned.
